title: arXiv Trending Physics — Daily, 2026-09-30
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending or usage ranking. This ordering is inferred from concrete result strength, breadth across subfields, cross-listing, measurement/data relevance and recency; it is not a readership or download ranking. Independent attention evidence and citation evidence are sparse for this fresh batch.

sections.title: Search for compressed electroweak SUSY production in final states with two τ-leptons in √s = 13 and 13.6 TeV pp collisions with the ATLAS detector
sections.abstract: ATLAS searches for compressed stau and electroweakino production in Run 2 and Run 3 proton collisions, finding results broadly consistent with the Standard Model alongside several 2.1–2.4σ local deviations.
sections.claimed_result: Reports 95% CL limits for selected mass-splitting scenarios, including electroweakino masses up to 200 GeV and pure chargino masses up to 175 GeV; no combined-channel exclusion is obtained for direct stau production.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; ATLAS LHC collision data recorded in 2015–2018 and 2022–2023.
sections.unique_caveat: The deviations are local (2.1–2.4σ) and results are generally consistent with the Standard Model; this is not a discovery claim.

sections.title: Measurements of the inclusive Branching fractions of the D_s^+ → η(η′) X decays
sections.abstract: BESIII measures inclusive D_s^+ branching fractions to ηX and η′X as 30.72% and 12.30%, respectively, with statistical and systematic uncertainties, improving on earlier precision.
sections.claimed_result: Using BESIII data at √s = 4.128–4.226 GeV, reports B(D_s^+→ηX)=(30.72±0.90±0.46)% and B(D_s^+→η′X)=(12.30±0.94±0.37)%, with statistical then systematic uncertainties.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; BESIII e⁺e⁻ collision sample, analyzed with single- and double-tag reconstruction.
sections.unique_caveat: Results are consistent with earlier CLEO measurements; uncertainties remain and the inclusive determination depends on tag reconstruction and systematic treatment.

sections.title: Constraining dark matter using 20-year INTEGRAL/IBIS observations II: Sub-GeV dark matter
sections.abstract: The authors combine spatial profiles and hard-X-ray spectra from 20 years of INTEGRAL/IBIS observations to set sub-GeV dark-matter annihilation and decay limits, reporting improvements of up to two orders of magnitude over prior X-ray bounds across much of the range.
sections.claimed_result: For e⁺e⁻, μ⁺μ⁻ and π⁺π⁻ channels from 1 MeV to 5 GeV, derives 95% upper limits on annihilation and decay and translates them to dark-photon and scalar-portal parameters.
sections.evidence_type: Observational analysis; INTEGRAL/IBIS diffuse hard-X-ray spectra and Galactic longitudinal profiles from observations spanning 2003–2024.
sections.unique_caveat: Inference depends on astrophysical background and propagation models, including cosmic-ray-electron inverse-Compton emission and unresolved accreting white dwarfs.

sections.title: One-dimensional quantum Gibbs states in constant circuit depth
sections.abstract: Proves an exact block-product mixture decomposition for 1D spin-chain Gibbs states at constant temperature, implying constant-depth preparation and strict bounds on several forms of thermal entanglement.
sections.claimed_result: For any spin chain at constant temperature, Gibbs states admit an exact bounded-block product-state mixture; an analogous constant-depth decomposition is given for local 1D fermionic Hamiltonians.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; mathematical proof, with implications for 1D many-body state preparation and dynamics.
sections.unique_caveat: Results concern one-dimensional local systems at constant temperature and do not establish the same structure for higher-dimensional systems or arbitrary low-temperature regimes.

sections.title: Deciding the Attainability of the Multiparameter Quantum Fisher Information is NP-Hard
sections.abstract: Proves that deciding whether individual-copy measurements can attain the multiparameter quantum Fisher-information bound is NP-hard, even for a restricted class of real, constant-rank models.
sections.claimed_result: A reduction from bipartite-state separability establishes NP-hardness for exact attainability decisions in the restricted model class.
sections.unique_caveat: The hardness proof applies to specified real, constant-rank models and individual-copy measurements; it does not rule out efficient criteria for narrower structured physical families.

sections.title: Advancing Fuzzy-Sphere CFTs: SO(3)-Rotation-Resolving Exact Diagonalization, 3D Ising Heavy Primaries, and Quasi-Hole-Space Projection
sections.abstract: Uses rotational-symmetry-resolved exact diagonalization to reduce fuzzy-sphere computation costs by factors of several hundred, identify roughly 100 primaries in the 3D Ising CFT, and propose a reduced quasi-hole basis for CFTs linked to fractional quantum Hall states.
sections.claimed_result: Reports resolving a prior tension over a parity-odd scalar primary and identifying heavy scalar primaries up to Δ≈16.5; proposes quasi-hole-space projection for CFTs intertwined with topological order.
sections.evidence_type: Computational/theoretical; symmetry-resolved exact diagonalization and finite-size quantum Hall model spaces.
sections.unique_caveat: Spectrum and operator identification come from numerical finite-size regularization, making continuum interpretation and extrapolation method-dependent.

sections.title: A parameter independent analysis of the QCD chiral phase transition and its universal critical behaviour
sections.abstract: Analyzes scaling behavior in (2+1)-flavor lattice-QCD simulations to estimate chiral-transition parameters and quantify departures from expected universal scaling as the light-to-strange quark-mass ratio changes.
sections.claimed_result: Using highly improved staggered fermions with temporal extent Nτ=8, estimates transition temperature and critical parameters directly from simulations and quantifies scaling deviations.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; (2+1)-flavor lattice-QCD simulations over multiple volumes and light-quark masses.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports Nτ=8 simulations and a proceedings contribution; continuum-extrapolation and finite-lattice effects remain important before treating parameter estimates as final.

sections.title: Low Frequency Gravitational Wave Detection with Gravito-Magnetism
sections.abstract: Proposes measuring the gravito-magnetic component of low-frequency gravitational waves through test-body Lorentz acceleration in a three-satellite constellation to distinguish signals from asteroid-belt gravity-gradient noise.
sections.claimed_result: Argues that gravito-magnetic acceleration can separate 10 nHz–1 μHz gravitational-wave signals from asteroid-induced Newtonian gravity-gradient noise in a three-satellite setup.
sections.evidence_type: Forecast/proposal; theoretical signal-separation analysis and a proposed atom-interferometer proof-mass reference.
sections.unique_caveat: Requires a proof mass isolated from non-gravitational noise; no instrument demonstration or gravitational-wave detection is reported.
